data.name: Motabir
data.gender_notes: Motabir is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The one who explains or settles disputes. Derived from the Arabic root 't-b-r', meaning 'to explain' or 'to judge'. In Islamic history, Motabir was a title given to scholars and judges who were known for their wisdom and fairness. The name Motabir carries the meaning “Explainer, Arbiter” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Motabir usually hope their child will grow to embody explainer, arbiter and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that symbolizes knowledge, wisdom, and the pursuit of truth.
data.etymology: Motabir belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Explainer, Arbiter.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Motabir total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The title Motabir has a significant cultural impact in the Islamic world, representing the importance of knowledge, wisdom, and justice. In many Islamic communities, Motabir were esteemed figures who were sought-after for their expertise in religious and secular matters. They played a crucial role in spreading knowledge, settling disputes, and upholding the moral values of society. The tradition of having Motabir in most Islamic countries continues even today, highlighting the importance of education, wisdom, and fairness in maintaining social harmony.
data.spiritual_significance: The title Motabir holds profound spiritual significance in the Islamic context, symbolizing the ideals of truth, guidance, and justice. Motabir were not just scholars or judges, but were also considered to be spiritual guides and steerers of the moral compass of their communities. They were expected to embody the qualities of patience, compassion, fairness, and knowledge, and to use their wisdom to help others navigate the complexities of life. Motabir were believed to have a close connection with the divine and were tasked with helping others draw closer to Allah by following the righteous path. In this sense, the title Motabir encapsulates the spiritual ideal of being a servant of the community, using knowledge, wisdom, and compassion to help others on their spiritual journey.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Abd al-Hakam's account of the fifth Caliph, Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan, mentions Motabir ibn Abbad al-Thaqafi as the governor of Kufa during the early Umayyad period.
historical_references.context: Motabir played a significant role in the political and administrative affairs of the Umayyad Caliphate during this period.

historical_references.reference: Al-Baladhuri's 'Ansab al-Ashraf' records Motabir ibn Abbad al-Thaqafi as one of the prominent leaders of the Banu Thaqif tribe during the early Islamic period. He was a noted poet and scholar, and was also a transmitter of Hadith.
historical_references.context: Motabir's contributions to Islamic literature and scholarship are significant, especially in the context of the early development of Islamic thought and culture.
